note: THE STEP RECORD'S SHAPE, AND THE TEXT THE MODEL IS SHOWN BEFORE IT
COMPOSES ONE (kogaki#1108).
WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR, stated first because it is what separates it from
every other schema carrier in src/. The other schemas are read by a
validator and by nothing else: they describe a record the composing party
already knows the shape of. This one is read TWICE, and the second reader
is the point. `validateSteps` in src/compose.mjs reads the field set from
it, and the path-composition state of the Brief workflow table RENDERS it
into the judge's prompt. So the text the Model composes against and the
text the refusal enforces are one file and cannot disagree.
THE DEFECT THIS CLOSES, measured on 2026-09-12 over the two live Briefs
(theses/calling-saved-permission-durable-leaves and
theses/steps-real-quality-matter-degree). No file declared the Step's
fields or what they mean. The composer inferred the shape from
.claude/skills/brief/SKILL.md's prose, wrote a Candidates JSON, and
`validateSteps` checked it afterwards -- so the only Harness text carrying
what a field means was a refusal string, seen only when shape had already
failed. Ground cardinality drifted accordingly: the first Brief carried 1
to 3 grounds per Step, the second 4 to 6, with up to six grounds from one
Strand in a single Step.
IT DECLARES SHAPE AND MEANING, AND JUDGES NEITHER. Every MUST of the
composition design stays judgment-class and is judged at path review. A
missing field is refused here; a weak rationale is not, and no description
below is ever matched against a value.
SPEC REFERENCES IN THIS FILE (kogaki#902; one carrier, kogaki#982).
The rule these entries are written under -- what a copy is, what the two
markers `[implemented-against: ...]` and `[see: ...]` mean, and why nothing
names a section number or a line range -- lives in ONE place:
`src/SPEC-REFERENCES.md`. It is not restated here.

what_a_step_is: A Step is one move of the Reader Path: the smallest unit that takes the
reader from one state to another. `Step = Input + State` -- the Input is
the material it stands on (its Strands), and the State is the Move it
binds, which is what names the kind of reader-state transition it makes.
A Step with no Move has no defined transition type and is not a Step.

step_id.description: This Step's own id, unique within the path. Other Steps address it through `depends_on`, and the specialization record carries one verdict per id.

materials.description: The Strands this Step stands on, as LessonDisplayIDs (`L<n>`). A Step with no material asserts nothing on anyone's behalf.

purpose.description: What this Step is for in the path -- the work it does toward the adopted Thesis, in one or two sentences.

reader_state_before.description: What the reader holds when this Step begins. Judged at the specialization occasion against the Move's `requires`: a Step's before-state must be a consistent specialization of what its Move demands.

reader_state_after.description: What the reader holds when this Step ends. Judged against the Move's `effect` the same way. The two state fields are the Step's transition, written as the reader's condition rather than as the writer's intent.

depends_on.description: The EARLIER Steps whose conclusions this Step stands on, by `step_id`. May be empty. An id that is not an earlier Step is refused -- a dependency on a later Step is a path that cannot be read in order.

rationale.description: Why this Step sits HERE, at this position, rather than earlier or later. The order argument, not a restatement of the purpose.

move.description: The Move library entry this Step binds, by id. The Move IS the State component of a Step, so the binding is required rather than encouraged, and the id is resolved against the Move library at adoption.

grounds.description: What this Step asserts, one entry per Strand it names in `materials`. See `ground` below -- the cardinality rule is the part most likely to be got wrong.

entailed.description: True where a proposition this Step asserts is not explicit in the material and is reached by inference. The flag is the composer's judgment; the Harness refuses only a flag with no reasoning beside it.

entailment_reasoning.description: The inference itself, stated so path review and the owner can judge it. Entailment is interpretation, judged rather than silently trusted.

bridges.description: Present only on a Step inserted between two adjacent Steps during the revise pass; names that adjacent pair by `step_id`. It is disclosed at the Candidate-selection gate, so an unvalidated marking would render at an owner surface.

introduces.description: Terms this Step introduces to the reader for the first time. The accumulated ledger the Step Packet renders is derived from these; whether a term is genuinely new HERE is a judgment and is not checked.

opens_section.description: Present on a Step that opens a Section of the finished article; carries that Section's name. The four grouping rules are a property of the whole path and run after every Step is known to be well formed.

figure.description: The composer's statement of what a figure lets the reader hold here that the prose leaves hard to hold. The default is NO figure: a Step without this field has none and nothing asks about it.

figure_roles.description: Binds every role of the Move's `visual_form` to one of THIS Step's own grounds, addressed `g<n>` and numbered from 1 in the order the grounds are declared. A role bound to another Step's ground is unreachable by construction: the address space is this Step's grounds and has no syntax for anyone else's.

definition: A GROUND IS THE ONE PROPOSITION THIS STEP ASSERTS ON BEHALF OF ONE
STRAND, FOR THIS READER AT THIS POINT IN THE PATH.
ONE GROUND PER STRAND NAMED IN `materials`. Two grounds in one Step
naming the same Strand is REFUSED, naming the Step and the Strand. A
Strand that serves several Steps carries a DIFFERENT ground in each --
that is what makes the path a sequence rather than a restatement, and it
is why the rule is per Step rather than per path.
WHY THE CARDINALITY IS BOUNDED AT ALL, measured rather than argued
(kogaki#1108). The Step Packet requires every declared ground to be
recoverable from the realized passage, and `grounds-unused` fails the
Step otherwise. With cardinality unbounded, ground generation drifted
into composing the article's decisive lines wholesale and calling them
grounds -- so the comparison the Packet performs stopped measuring
grounding and started measuring how much of the passage had been written
in advance. One proposition per Strand is what keeps a ground a claim
the Strand supports rather than a draft of the sentence that will carry
it.
A GROUND IS ONE CLAIM DERIVED FROM A STRAND, AND NOTHING ELSE. The type
set is closed at `strand`. Inherited reader state belongs to
`reader_state_before` and to the computed `already knows` ledger; a
presupposed premise belongs to the Brief's Reader start. Neither is an
assertion, so a passage that realizes its Step correctly never states
one and the Blind Reader never recovers it.

retired_types.step_effect: inherited reader state, which is already carried by this Step's `reader_state_before` and by the computed `already knows` ledger
retired_types.reader_assumption: a presupposed premise, which belongs to the Brief's Reader start

type.description: The closed set above. Today it has one member, `strand`.

proposition.description: The claim itself, STATED -- a specific proposition this Step asserts, not a pointer at where one could be found. An untyped pointer is not a ground.

strand.description: The Strand this ground derives from, as a LessonDisplayID (`L<n>`). It is one of this Step's `materials`, and no other ground of this Step names it.

what_is_judged_elsewhere: Nothing here is a lint over a judgment. Whether a rationale is good,
whether a ground is genuinely supported by its Strand, whether a term is
really introduced here, and whether the before/after states are faithful
specializations of the Move are all judgment-class: they are judged at
